comments.text_zh: > 比如说 JS，我该怎么学，才能学到真正开窍、写程序时能在脑子里想象出底层在发生什么的程度？去了解 JS 引擎是怎么工作的。哪个引擎都行，不过 V8 在网上讨论得最多。可以从这几样入手：- 事件循环是怎么工作的（[VIDEO]）。它展示了 JS 底层如何运作，哪些属于“JS”本身、哪些是扩展，异步操作如何在单线程上被调度。看完之后，一切都会“咔哒”一下贯通。- V8 里对象是如何表示的（[LINK]）。这是 V8 特有的，但它仍然能告诉你对象在内存里是怎么表示的。把这些概念记在心里，你从一开始就能写出高效的代码。- ES6 规范（[LINK]）。可选阅读（如果你想读 500 多页的话），但有疑问时它是个顺手好用的参考。你完全可以把这东西甩给一个根本不知道自己在说什么的人。倒不是说你真该这么做，但手里有据可依总是好的。
comments.text: > How do I take, say JS, and learn it to the point where it really clicks to the point where I can visualize what's going on under the hood when I write programs? Learn how a JS engine works. Any engine will do, although V8 is very discussed on the internet. Here's a few things to get started with: - How the event loop works ( [VIDEO] ). This show how JS works under the hood, what's part of "JS" and what's extended, how async operations are scheduled on a single thread. After watching this, everything will just "click". - How objects are represented in V8 ( [LINK] ). It's v8-specific but nevertheless tells you how objects are represented in memory. Keeping these concepts in mind, you will be able to write efficient code on the get-go. - ES6 spec ( [LINK] ). Optional reading (if you want to read 500+ pages), but it's a handy reference when in doubt. You can literally slap this thing to a person who doesn't know what they're talking about. Not that you should, but backing evidence is always great.

comments.why_zh: 关于理解异步 JS 的部分建议。
comments.text_zh: 完全同意。除了学习这门语言的基础（如果你已经会任何其他“类 C”语言，这并不难），真正理解异步流程（先是 Promises，然后是 async/await）在 JS 中绝对关键，而且可能是我见到人们最常卡住的地方。在我工作的地方，我被当成 JS“专家”，我的同事包括几位年纪较大的资深工程师，他们主要做后端，认为 JS 是糟糕/令人困惑的语言；还有几位初级工程师，他们真正有经验的只是在学校学过的语言（其中大概不包括 JS）。我帮他们解决的问题中，90% 都是因为不理解异步 JS——“为什么这个值是 undefined？”或者“我怎么把数据从 Promise 里取出来？”而对于后一种，我告诉他们“嗯，你不是把数据从 Promise 里取出来，而是用 .then(data => data) 把它串起来，以便操作/使用数据”，通常换来的是更困惑的表情。虽然 async/await 对他们如何使用已完成的异步操作返回的数据帮助很大，你仍然需要（至少稍微）理解 promises，因为它是建立在 promises 之上的（例如，在 try/catch 的 async 块中，await 之后的行本质上就是传给 promise.then() 的函数，而 catch 块中的行就是传给 promise.catch() 的函数）。另外还有两件事我想提一下（可以归在“学习这门语言”下面），我认为它们对真正理解 JS 并把它用好很有帮助
comments.text: Completely agree. Aside from learning the basics of the language (which if you already know any other "C like" language isn't difficult), gaining a good understanding of async flows (Promises then async/await) is absolutely key in JS and is probably the biggest hangup I see people run into. Where I work I'm considered the JS "expert", my coworkers consist of a few older seniors that mostly do backend work that think JS is bad/confusing language, and a few juniors that really only have experience with languages they learned in school (which probably doesn't include JS). And 90% of the issues I help them with are caused by a lack of understanding of async JS -- "why is this value undefined?" or "how do I get the data out of a Promise" and for the latter telling them "well, you don't get the data out of a Promise, you would chain it with .then(data => data) to operate/use the data" is usually met with even more confused looks. Though async/await helps a ton with how they use the data from a resolved async operation, you still need to understand promises (at least a little) since it's built on top of them (e.g. in a try/catch async block the lines after the await are essentially the function that gets passed to promise.then() and the lines in the catch block being the function that gets passed to promise.catch()).
